description: The Cosmic Scribe is a solo storytelling project for NASA's "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Using NASA's open data, this project transforms raw telemetry and logs from inactive rovers and probes on Mars and the Moon into immersive digital chronicles. Designed for school-age enthusiasts, it crafts a 240-second video narrative tracking the history and legacy of these lonely machine pioneers. Based in Dhaka, it focuses on high-impact minimalism and data-driven storytelling.
summary: Echoes of the Cosmos (Project THE COSMIC SCRIBE) is an interactive educational storytelling platform designed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to NASA’s forgotten off-world artifacts. Since the 1960s, numerous rovers, landers, and deep-space probes have remained silent on the Moon, Mars, and beyond, with their histories buried inside dense technical archives. Our project transforms real NASA mission datasets into engaging, accessible narratives that highlight the engineering behind these robotic explorers and the groundbreaking scientific discoveries they achieved. By bringing these silent machines back to life through interactive storytelling, Echoes of the Cosmos bridges the gap between complex space history and young learners, inspiring the next generation of explorers globally.
details: Echoes of the Cosmos is an interactive educational storytelling platform designed for school-age space enthusiasts to explore NASA’s off-world artifacts. Since the 1960s, numerous rovers, landers, and probes have been left on the Moon, Mars, and deep space after completing their missions. We transformed complex technical data from NASA’s Planetary Data System (PDS), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), and NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) into accessible, story-driven experiences. Users can click on historic hardware—such as Apollo rovers, Mars landers, and Voyager probes—to learn why they were built, how they operated, and what scientific discoveries they made possible.
